items.title: Chico Freeman interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2001
items.q: they’d be rehearsing with my dad and his bands. Don Baldwin, Andrew Hill, Vernel Fournier.

ctx.x: Well naturally, like any kid, teenager, you grow up listening to the music that you grow up listening to, so I was no different. So at first it was R&B, rhythm & blues, all the singing groups, because I actually sang in a singing group. I had my own singing group. I sang in a few — did all the talent shows in high school. So I was listening to R&B, which would be Motown and the Drifters and things like that. Coming from Chicago, there was groups like the Impressions, Curtis Mayfield, Jerry Butler, you know the…
they’d be rehearsing with my dad and his bands. Don Baldwin, Andrew Hill, Vernel Fournier.
Wow. Now these guys are pretty modern players too. I guess I had this impression, I have to readjust my thinking, that they were pretty up to date. In other words they were not just playing swing.
